name: JFK Assassination Conspiracy Theories
description: The most-studied assassination in history. The Warren Commission (1964) found Oswald acted alone; the House Select Committee on Assassinations (1979) concluded a second gunman was 'probable' on acoustic evidence later disputed. Polls have long shown most Americans doubt the lone-gunman account, and periodic document releases keep the debate alive without producing proof of a plot.

name: Moon Landing Hoax
description: Popularized by Bill Kaysing's 1976 self-published book. Refuted by independent evidence: 382 kg of lunar samples analysed worldwide, retroreflectors still used for laser ranging, Soviet tracking that would have exposed fraud, and modern orbiter photographs of the landing sites. A standard case study in conspiratorial reasoning.

name: Roswell UFO Incident Theories
description: The Army first announced a 'flying disc', then a weather balloon. The 1994 Air Force report identified the debris as Project Mogul — a classified balloon array for detecting Soviet nuclear tests — and 'bodies' as later anthropomorphic test dummies. The incident, revived by ufologists in the late 1970s, remains the anchor of UFO conspiracy culture.

name: Area 51 Alien Technology
description: The secrecy is real — Area 51 developed the U-2, A-12/SR-71, and stealth aircraft, and the CIA only acknowledged the base in 2013 — which explains decades of unexplained sightings. Bob Lazar's 1989 claims of working on alien propulsion made the base world-famous; no physical evidence has ever corroborated the alien component.

name: Modern Flat Earth Theory
description: Rowbotham's Victorian 'Zetetic Astronomy' revived by online communities. Sphericity is directly observable (ship hulls, star declinations, circumnavigating flights, satellite imagery) and was measured by Eratosthenes c. 240 BCE. Notable as a case where the conspiracy must grow to include essentially everyone.

name: Chemtrails
description: Contrail persistence depends on humidity and temperature at altitude — a phenomenon documented since the 1940s. A 2016 survey of 77 atmospheric scientists found none who had encountered evidence of a spraying program. Real geoengineering research (stratospheric aerosols) is discussed openly in scientific literature, which the theory conflates with covert operations.

name: New World Order
description: A meta-theory absorbing others — banking dynasties, secret societies, the UN, Davos. Its explanatory flexibility is its weakness: any event confirms it. Scholars treat it as the modern template of the 'superconspiracy', with roots in anti-Masonic and antisemitic literature that responsible discussion must acknowledge.

name: Illuminati Survival Theory
description: The historical Illuminati was a real Enlightenment society (founded 1776 by Adam Weishaupt) banned within a decade. Barruel and Robison blamed it for the French Revolution, founding the modern genre of conspiracy literature. No evidence of institutional survival exists; the name persists as pop-culture shorthand for hidden power.

name: 9/11 Inside-Job Theories
description: The 9/11 Commission and NIST's engineering investigations attributed the attacks to al-Qaeda and the collapses to impact damage and uncontrolled fires (WTC 7: fire-induced failure of a critical column). Genuine documented failures — ignored warnings, inter-agency dysfunction — are distinct from complicity, a distinction the literature on the movement emphasizes.

name: Paul Is Dead
description: A campus-newspaper rumor that became a mass phenomenon of reverse-played lyrics and album-cover exegesis (the Abbey Road 'funeral procession'). McCartney's continued, verifiable existence makes it the classic benign example of clue-hunting pattern-mania.

name: Extended MKUltra Theories
description: The documented core is real: MKUltra (1953–1973) dosed unwitting subjects with LSD among 149 subprojects, and Director Helms destroyed most records in 1973 — the destruction itself fueling maximal speculation. Claims beyond the surviving record (successful 'Manchurian candidates', ongoing programs) remain unevidenced; the affair is the canonical proof that some conspiracies are real, which theorists generalize.

name: Philadelphia Experiment
description: Originated in letters from Carl Allen ('Carlos Allende') to a UFO author; Allen later admitted invention. Ship's logs place the Eldridge elsewhere on the claimed dates. Likely garbled from real degaussing research (making ships undetectable to magnetic mines, not eyes).

name: Hollow Earth Theory
description: Proposed seriously by Edmond Halley (1692) to explain compass anomalies, elaborated by Symmes in the 1810s, and attached to later polar-expedition myths. Seismology settled the interior's structure — solid inner core, liquid outer core — a century ago.

name: Reptilian Elite
description: Popularized by David Icke from 1999. Notable to researchers chiefly as an absorbing-boundary of conspiracy belief and for survey findings that a measurable percentage of respondents endorse it; critics also note its capacity to encode older antisemitic tropes beneath science-fiction imagery.

name: Denver Airport Conspiracy
description: The airport's oddities are real and mundane: Tanguma's peace-and-environment murals, a time capsule with a Masonic marker, an automated-baggage tunnel system that famously failed. The airport now cheerfully markets the legend. A model case of ambiguous public art feeding narrative construction.

name: HAARP Weather-Control Theories
description: HAARP's 3.6 MW heats a small patch of ionosphere to study radio propagation — energy many orders of magnitude below weather systems, and physically incapable of coupling to tectonics. The facility, now run by the University of Alaska, holds open houses. A staple attribution after any natural disaster.

name: Water Fluoridation Conspiracy
description: Fluoridation at ~0.7 ppm reduces tooth decay and is endorsed by major public-health bodies; legitimate scientific debate concerns optimal dosing, not conspiracies. The Cold-War version was immortalized by General Ripper in Dr. Strangelove.

name: Majestic 12
description: Rests on documents mailed anonymously on film to a UFO researcher in 1984. The FBI declared them 'completely bogus'; internal anachronisms (format, typeface, an incorrect Truman signature lifted from another letter) mark them as forgeries. MJ-12 nonetheless became load-bearing lore for later UFO claims.

name: Shakespeare Authorship Question
description: Arose from Victorian incredulity that a glover's son could write the canon. Mainstream scholarship is essentially unanimous for Shakespeare, resting on contemporary attributions, theatrical records, and stylometric analysis; the debate persists as the classic 'genteel' conspiracy theory.

name: Phantom Time Hypothesis
description: Heribert Illig's hypothesis fails against independent chronologies: dendrochronology, recorded solar eclipses matching astronomical retro-calculation, Tang-dynasty and Islamic records synchronized with European ones, and radiocarbon dating. A vivid illustration of how interlocking evidence anchors chronology.

name: Tartaria / Mud Flood
description: 'Tartary' was simply the old European label for Central Asian lands, not a hidden civilization. The theory reinterprets demolished world's-fair buildings and basement windows as evidence of a global 'mud flood' cover-up. A born-digital myth notable for spreading through image boards and video essays.

name: Birds Aren't Real
description: A deliberate parody movement created by Peter McIndoe to satirize conspiracy culture from within — complete with billboards and rallies. Included here as the reference example of ironic/satirical 'conspiracy' and of how style can outrun substance online.

name: Lunar Wave / Hologram Moon
description: The 'lunar wave' artefacts are atmospheric distortion and camera rolling-shutter effects. Cited by researchers as an example of raw-footage artefacts being elevated into cosmology.

name: Dead Internet Theory
description: The strong claim (a coordinated takeover dating to ~2016) is unevidenced; the weak claim tracks real measurements — bot traffic rivaling human traffic, synthetic content proliferating post-2022. Interesting as a theory whose plausibility rose after its invention due to generative AI.

name: Operation Mockingbird (Extended Claims)
description: Documented core: Church Committee findings and Carl Bernstein's 1977 reporting showed the CIA maintained relationships with hundreds of journalists during the Cold War. 'Mockingbird' as a formal, continuing, all-encompassing program is an extrapolation beyond the record; the name itself appears only for an unrelated small wiretap operation.

name: Titanic/Olympic Switch
description: Refuted by hull-number evidence on wreck components, insurance records (Titanic was under-insured relative to cost), and the logistical impossibility of secretly swapping thousands of fitted parts. A model 'insurance-scam' template applied to a famous disaster.

name: Polybius
description: No contemporary evidence of the cabinet exists; the story first appears decades later and blends real 1981 events (arcade FBI raids over gambling, a player illness at a marathon session). The canonical video-game creepypasta studied as modern folklore.

name: Finland Doesn't Exist
description: Began as a deliberately absurd Reddit thought experiment about believing things without first-hand verification, then circulated as if sincere. Useful as a clean specimen of ironic belief propagation.

name: Project Blue Beam
description: Advanced by journalist Serge Monast without documentation. Perpetually predicted, never occurring; each new sky phenomenon (drone swarms, satellite trains) is folded into it. The archetype of prophecy-style technological conspiracy.

name: Suppressed Cancer Cures
description: Incompatible with the structure of medicine: cancer is hundreds of diseases; researchers and their families die of it; a real cure would be worth fortunes and fame. The theory's persistence reflects genuine grievances about drug pricing and trial transparency, redirected into a simpler villain narrative. Harmful when it diverts patients from treatment.

name: Crop Circle Theories
description: Doug Bower and Dave Chorley demonstrated in 1991 how they had made hundreds with planks and rope since 1976; circle-making teams now produce openly commissioned formations of great complexity. Residual claims focus on formations asserted to be too intricate — an unfalsifiable remainder.

name: Hollow / Artificial Moon
description: Traces to a 1970 speculative article by two Soviet writers proposing the Moon as an alien ark. Seismic 'ringing' from Apollo-era impacts reflects a dry, rigid interior, not hollowness; lunar gravity mapping fully constrains a solid body.

name: Nazi Antarctic Base 211
description: Germany's single 1938–39 Antarctic expedition mapped coastline for whaling claims and landed no infrastructure. Operation Highjump (1946–47) was a US training and territorial exercise. Ties into 'Nazi survival' myth-making around escaped war criminals who in reality fled to South America.

name: Avril Lavigne Replacement
description: Created by a Brazilian fan blog explicitly to demonstrate how easily conspiracy 'evidence' (photo comparisons, lyric readings) can be manufactured — then widely believed anyway. The clearest documented case of a theory outliving its own disclaimer.
